intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry, and you can stroll through the stunning courtyards, visit the National Folk Museum inside, and capture iconic K-drama-worthy photos at the palace gates and pavilions.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Seoul's oldest traditional market and feast on iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with grandmothers who have been running their stalls for decades for an authentic local culinary experience.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Experience & SM Town COEX Artium
experiences.description: Visit SM Town COEX Artium, a flagship K-pop cultural complex dedicated to SM Entertainment artists like EXO, aespa, and SHINee. Explore interactive exhibits, hologram performances, and a K-pop merchandise store. Afterward, head to nearby Apgujeong Rodeo Street to spot entertainment agency buildings and experience the glamorous K-culture lifestyle district.

experiences.name: Insadong & Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Bukchon Hanok Village, a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean wooden houses (hanok) with sweeping views of the city. Continue to Insadong for traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and street snacks like hotteok (sweet pancakes). This walk offers an immersive blend of living heritage and artisan culture.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ & Soju Night in Hongdae
experiences.description: Experience the quintessential Korean dining ritual of samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs) at a lively BBQ restaurant in the youthful Hongdae district. Pair your meal with soju and makgeolli, then explore the vibrant street performances, indie music venues, and K-pop dance crews that make Hongdae the heartbeat of youth K-culture in Seoul.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs and immigration, exchange some currency at the airport (rates are decent), and pick up a T-money card and a pocket WiFi or SIM card at the airport convenience store or telecom booth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) all-city train to Hongik University Station, then transfer to Line 3 toward Gyeongbokgung Station (total ~70 min, ~₩4,150). Check in to your boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, drop your luggage, and take a short walk to nearby Gyeongbokgung Palace exterior to get oriented — admire the Gwanghwamun Gate area and the surrounding Joseon-era walls at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong-gil (Insadong Street), just a 15-minute walk from the hotel — browse traditional craft shops, galleries, and street stalls. Grab dinner in the Insadong area and wind down after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at Incheon Airport convenience store (GS25 or CU) — kimbap rolls or triangle gimbap for ~₩1,500–₩2,500.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab airport convenience store food (budget ~₩5,000) since you land at 13:00 and will be in transit.
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang area or a local pojangmacha (street food tent) near Insadong — try tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), eomuk (fish cake soup skewers), and hotteok (sweet pancakes) for ~₩5,000–₩8,000 total.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Don't over-schedule — jet lag may be real. December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C typical), so layer up immediately upon landing. Keep your T-money card topped up (₩20,000–₩30,000 to start).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — right at your doorstep! Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the Gwanghwamun Gate (held at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM, free to watch). Explore the vast palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon (throne hall) and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion. Entry: ₩3,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village — a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses with mountain and palace views. It's free to walk through. Then head to nearby Changdeokgung Palace (UNESCO World Heritage Site) for a self-guided tour. Entry: ₩3,000.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwangjang Market (광장시장) via subway (Line 1, Jongno 5-ga Station) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. Explore the indoor food stalls for a true local night market experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel (CU or GS25) — banana milk, egg sandwich, and instant coffee for ~₩3,000–₩4,000.
meals.lunch: Snack inside Gyeongbokgung or buy street food near the palace gate — hotteok or bungeoppang (fish-shaped pastry with red bean) for ~₩2,000.
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — must-try: mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls, ~₩3,000), bindaetteok (mung bean pancake, ~₩4,000), and yukhoe (beef tartare if budget allows, ~₩10,000). Full meal under ₩10,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear very warm clothes — palace grounds are exposed and windy in December. Renting a hanbok at the palace entrance (~₩15,000–₩20,000/hour) gives you free palace entry and great photo opportunities — optional but fun.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located a short walk from the hotel. Free to enter. Admire the intricate lanterns, architecture, and peaceful courtyard. Then walk to nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a restored urban stream with a pleasant walking path, free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — an iconic futuristic building designed by Zaha Hadid. The exterior and public spaces are free. Explore the surrounding Dongdaemun Market area, one of the world's largest fashion and fabric markets. Browse the stalls for affordable K-fashion finds.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun area comes alive at night — the shopping malls (Doota, Migliore) open until 5 AM. Window shop or buy affordable K-fashion items. Explore the outdoor night market stalls around DDP for street food.

meals.breakfast: Nearby local bakery (Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours) — coffee and pastry for ~₩4,000–₩5,000.
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — find a local bunsik (Korean snack restaurant) for a set meal of ramyeon + kimbap for ~₩6,000–₩8,000.
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun street food stalls — tteokbokki, sundae (Korean blood sausage), fried snacks combo for ~₩6,000–₩8,000. Or try a nearby 24-hour Korean restaurant for a hearty sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set for ~₩9,000.

day_by_day.notes: Cheonggyecheon Stream has winter light festivals in December — check if the Seoul Lantern Festival is still running (usually ends mid-December) for a magical free experience. Dongdaemun markets are best visited in the afternoon and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) area — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Walk through Hongik University's surrounding streets, check out the free street art murals, and browse the unique independent boutiques and vintage clothing shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area — beautiful campus architecture, affordable shopping, and a vibrant café culture. Browse the underground shopping street in Sinchon for very affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the Friday night street performance scene — local buskers, K-pop cover dancers, and indie musicians perform in the main square (Hongdae Free Market area) and surrounding streets, completely free to watch. Soak in the youthful K-culture energy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store or a local Korean breakfast spot — doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set with rice for ~₩6,000–₩7,000.
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a local Korean fried chicken (chimaek) lunch special or a bibimbap restaurant for ~₩8,000–₩10,000.
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food and pojangmacha — ddeokbokki, twigim (fried snacks), and a cup of soju (~₩4,000 per bottle) for a classic Korean street food dinner under ₩10,000.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Hongdae are especially lively with street performers. The area is very walkable. Keep an eye out for free K-pop dance cover performances near the main Hongdae entrance plaza — a true K-culture experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower (남산타워) — take Bus 02 or 03 (Namsan Circular Bus, ~₩1,200) partway up, then walk the scenic trail to the top. The mountain park is free. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (tower entry: ₩21,000 — optional, the free outdoor deck area still has great views).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's famous shopping and street food district. Explore the main pedestrian street lined with K-beauty shops (free samples everywhere!), international brands, and street food vendors. Stock up on affordable Korean skincare products.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Myeongdong's evening street food scene — it's especially vibrant on weekends. Then walk to nearby Namdaemun Market (남대문시장), one of Korea's largest traditional markets, for evening shopping and food.

meals.breakfast: Local juk (Korean porridge) restaurant near the hotel — a warm, nourishing bowl for ~₩7,000–₩9,000, perfect for a cold December morning.
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — tornado potato, egg bread (계란빵), grilled lobster skewer, and Korean corn dog for a filling street food lunch under ₩10,000.
meals.dinner: Namdaemun Market — galchi jorim (braised cutlassfish) or a hearty haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake) at one of the traditional market restaurants for ~₩10,000–₩12,000.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day in Myeongdong — embrace the crowds, it's part of the experience. Many K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) offer significant discounts on weekends. Namdaemun Market closes early on Sundays, so Saturday evening is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) — a quieter, less-touristy royal palace adjacent to Changdeokgung. Entry: ₩1,000. Then walk through Naksan Park (낙산공원) — a hilltop park along the ancient Seoul City Wall (Hanyangdoseong) with beautiful views over the city and the Ihwa Mural Village below. All free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ihwa Mural Village (이화 벽화마을) — a charming hillside village famous for its street art murals, most notably the 'Fish out of Water' mural. Free to explore. Descend to Daehangno (대학로) — a cultural district known for theaters and university life, great for people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a trendy neighborhood of restored hanok houses turned into hip cafés, bars, and restaurants. Very Instagrammable and culturally rich. The narrow alleyways are magical in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local café near hotel — toast set with eggs and coffee for ~₩4,000–₩5,000.
meals.lunch: Daehangno area — a local Korean set meal (백반, baekban) at a neighborhood restaurant: rice, soup, and multiple banchan (side dishes) for ~₩7,000–₩8,000.
meals.dinner: Ikseon-dong — try a trendy but affordable Korean fusion café-restaurant. Look for tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties) or a warm sundubu jjigae set for ~₩9,000–₩12,000.

day_by_day.notes: Ikseon-dong is very popular among young Koreans and is a great place to experience the modern-meets-traditional K-culture aesthetic. Many cafés here serve traditional Korean desserts like bingsu (shaved ice) or sikhye (sweet rice punch) — warm versions available in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — take the subway from Gyeongbokgung to Suwon Station (Line 1, ~50 min, ~₩1,850). The UNESCO-listed fortress walls stretch 5.7 km around the city — walk the full circuit for stunning winter views. Entry: ₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional Haenggung Palace inside the fortress walls (entry: ₩1,500) and the surrounding traditional market area. Visit the Suwon Hwaseong Museum for cultural context (entry: ₩2,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Head to Noryangjin Fish Market (노량진수산시장) — one of Seoul's most exciting wholesale fish markets. Browse the massive selection of live seafood, choose your fish/shellfish from a vendor, pay a small processing fee (~₩5,000–₩8,000), and have it prepared fresh upstairs at a restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Quick convenience store meal before departing for Suwon — kimbap and banana milk for ~₩3,000.
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its galbi (grilled short ribs). Find an affordable galbi restaurant near the fortress for ~₩12,000–₩15,000 per person (a splurge but worth it for the local specialty).
meals.dinner: Noryangjin Fish Market — choose raw oysters, shrimp, or a small fish, pay the market price (varies, budget ~₩15,000–₩20,000 for a generous seafood meal including processing fee and rice).

day_by_day.notes: Hwaseong Fortress is beautiful in winter with snow-dusted walls — dress very warmly. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours. Noryangjin Fish Market is open 24 hours and is a uniquely Korean experience — very budget-friendly for the quality of seafood.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan — one of the world's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Entry is FREE. Plan to spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the adjacent National Museum of Korea garden (free, beautiful in winter). Then head to War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) — a sobering and comprehensive museum about Korean history and the Korean War. Entry is FREE. Very moving and educational.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's most international neighborhood with a diverse mix of cultures, cuisines, and nightlife. Walk the main Itaewon-daero and explore the side streets. Browse the vintage clothing shops on Antique Furniture Street.

meals.breakfast: Local Korean restaurant near hotel — haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty beef bone soup) for ~₩8,000–₩10,000, a warming winter breakfast.
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals for ~₩7,000–₩9,000, or bring a packed convenience store lunch to eat in the museum garden.
meals.dinner: Itaewon — explore the diverse food options. Try a local Korean BBQ spot just off the main street for samgyeopsal (pork belly) — look for restaurants with prices around ₩12,000–₩15,000 per person including rice and banchan.

day_by_day.notes: Both the National Museum and War Memorial are free and world-class — easily two of the best free attractions in Seoul. Itaewon has significantly revitalized since 2022 and is worth a visit for its unique multicultural atmosphere within Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관) — a powerful and important museum housed in the former Japanese colonial-era prison where Korean independence fighters were imprisoned. Entry: ₩3,000. A deeply moving cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hongdae area again but this time explore the KCDF Gallery (Korea Craft & Design Foundation) near Insadong for free exhibitions of traditional and contemporary Korean craft. Then visit Ssamziegil — a unique open courtyard shopping complex in Insadong with independent designers, craft shops, and performance spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural performance — check the Seoul Cultural Portal (culture.seoul.go.kr) for free traditional music (gugak) or dance performances. Many cultural centers near Gyeongbokgung offer free evening performances in December.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — try a local Korean breakfast restaurant for gyeran-bap (egg rice) or a simple doenjang jjigae set for ~₩6,000.
meals.lunch: Insadong area — Ssamziegil food court or nearby restaurant. Try a traditional Korean meal: doenjang jjigae + rice + banchan for ~₩8,000.
meals.dinner: Insadong-gil street food or a nearby local restaurant — try japchae (glass noodles with vegetables and meat) or a hearty kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) set for ~₩8,000–₩10,000.

day_by_day.notes: Seodaemun Prison is a sobering but essential cultural experience to understand modern Korean history and the independence movement. December 23rd — the city may begin Christmas decorations and events, adding a festive atmosphere to the Insadong area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) — a lesser-known but beautiful royal palace near the hotel, free entry. Then explore the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) right next door — a fascinating look at Seoul's transformation from ancient capital to modern megacity. Entry is FREE.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream again to see the Christmas decorations and winter illuminations. Head to City Hall Plaza (서울광장) — in December, the plaza is transformed into a massive outdoor ice skating rink and winter festival ground. Ice skating: ~₩1,000 entry + ~₩5,000 skate rental.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration — Myeongdong becomes incredibly festive with lights, carolers, and street performances. Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) holds Christmas Eve mass (free, open to all). The entire area is beautifully illuminated.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery — treat yourself to a Christmas-themed pastry and coffee for ~₩5,000.
meals.lunch: City Hall area — find a local Korean restaurant for a warm budae jjigae (army stew, a Korean-American fusion stew with ramen, spam, and vegetables) for ~₩10,000–₩12,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — Myeongdong area. Splurge slightly on a sit-down Korean BBQ or a hot pot restaurant for ~₩15,000–₩20,000 per person. Or enjoy the festive street food atmosphere for under ₩10,000.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday. Myeongdong Cathedral's Christmas mass is a beautiful cultural experience. The city is decorated magnificently. Book dinner early if going to a restaurant as it gets very busy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) — Seoul's stunning mountain national park within city limits. Take the subway to Gupabal Station or Dobongsan Station. Entry to the park is free. Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail (moderate difficulty, 2–3 hours) for incredible winter mountain and city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul and explore the hip Mangwon Market (망원시장) — a local neighborhood market beloved by young Koreans, less touristy than Gwangjang. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Yeouido Hangang Park (여의도한강공원) — Seoul's famous riverside park along the Han River. In December, it's cold but atmospheric, especially at night with city lights reflecting on the river. Grab convenience store snacks and enjoy the view.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store breakfast for the hike — kimbap, energy bars, and hot canned coffee for ~₩4,000–₩5,000.
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — try the famous Mangwon Market street food: jeon (savory pancakes), tteokbokki, and fresh fruit for ~₩6,000–₩8,000.
meals.dinner: Yeouido area — find a local Korean restaurant for samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) or galbitang (short rib soup) to warm up after an outdoor day for ~₩10,000–₩13,000.

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan in winter is beautiful but requires proper hiking gear — waterproof boots, warm layers, and gloves are essential. The park can be icy in December, so trekking poles are recommended. Most attractions are open on Christmas Day in Korea as it's a public holiday but not as intensely celebrated as in Western countries.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) — located inside the Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds, this excellent museum covers Korean traditional life, customs, and folk culture across the seasons. Entry is FREE (included with palace ticket or free on its own from the museum entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Garosu-gil (가로수길) in Gangnam — a tree-lined boulevard with trendy boutiques, concept stores, and cafés. Then head to nearby Sinsa-dong for window shopping and café culture. Take the subway to Gangnam Station and walk — experience the contrast between traditional and ultra-modern Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰) in Gangnam — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. The famous Starfield Library inside COEX (a stunning public library with massive bookshelves) is free to visit and perfect for photos. Browse the mall, see a movie at CGV (Korean cinema experience, ~₩10,000–₩14,000), or simply enjoy the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Last chance for a traditional Korean breakfast near the hotel — try a local restaurant for kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) for ~₩7,000.
meals.lunch: Garosu-gil area — find a trendy but affordable Korean restaurant. Try a Korean-style pasta or a modern bibimbap café for ~₩10,000–₩12,000.
meals.dinner: COEX food court or nearby Gangnam restaurant — try a Korean BBQ chain restaurant (Gopchang or samgyeopsal) for ~₩12,000–₩15,000 per person. Or explore the diverse COEX food court for under ₩10,000.

day_by_day.notes: Garosu-gil and Gangnam offer a completely different side of Seoul — ultra-modern, fashionable, and aspirational. The contrast with the traditional Gyeongbokgung area where you're staying is striking and culturally interesting. Starfield Library in COEX is free and one of Seoul's most photogenic spots.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite spot near the hotel for a peaceful farewell walk. Return to Gyeongbokgung Palace area at dawn for quiet, golden-hour photos without the crowds. Walk along the palace walls and through the Samcheong-dong neighborhood one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting at Insadong — pick up affordable traditional Korean souvenirs: hanji (traditional paper) crafts, ceramic tea cups, traditional fans, or gochujang (Korean chili paste) and doenjang (soybean paste) for foodie gifts. Namdaemun Market is also excellent for affordable last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Incheon Airport — take the AREX from Seoul Station (~43 min express, ₩9,500) or all-city train (~66 min, ₩4,150). Arrive at least 3 hours before your departure. Enjoy one final Korean meal at the airport — Incheon Airport has excellent food options including affordable Korean restaurants in the departure hall.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal near the hotel. Try a traditional Korean breakfast restaurant for a full set with rice, multiple soups, and banchan for ~₩8,000–₩10,000.
meals.lunch: Insadong area — a farewell meal of your favorite Korean dish discovered during the trip. Budget ~₩10,000–₩12,000.
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — Korean restaurant in the departure terminal. Try bibimbap or dosirak (Korean lunchbox set) for ~₩10,000–₩13,000 before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Pack any Korean instant ramen, snacks, or food souvenirs in your checked luggage (liquids like gochujang must be checked). Keep your T-money card — it can be used on future trips or refunded at the airport (machines near exit gates). Allow extra time at Incheon Airport on Sunday evenings as it can be very busy. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train (approx. 43 min) to Seoul Station, then transfer to Gyeongbokgung area. Check into the boutique stay in Jongno-gu.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a gentle orientation stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village (10-min walk from hotel). Wander the narrow alleyways lined with traditional hanok houses, soak in the atmosphere, and get your bearings in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Street (15-min walk) for a relaxed first evening. Browse the quirky shops, art galleries, and tea houses. Enjoy a warm cup of traditional Korean tea at a cozy café to shake off jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Seoul Station — try a convenience store kimbap or a bowl of ramen (approx. ₩3,000–5,000) while in transit
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — famous ginseng chicken soup, perfect comfort food after a long flight (approx. ₩17,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag from Europe (LH flight) will be significant. Prioritize hydration and a good night's sleep. Buy a T-money card at the airport or Seoul Station for easy transit use throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (right outside your hotel) for the morning — arrive early (9:00 AM) to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (held at 10:00 AM & 2:00 PM). Explore the grand palace grounds, Geunjeongjeon throne hall, and the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace (admission approx. ₩3,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Cheongwadae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence opened to the public. Take the free guided tour of the grounds and enjoy views of Bugaksan Mountain behind it. Then visit the nearby Cheongun-dong neighborhood for a scenic hillside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gwanghwamun Square at dusk — see the illuminated statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin and King Sejong. The square is beautifully lit in winter.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try a Korean-style breakfast with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste soup) and rice at a local restaurant (approx. ₩7,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Jongno-gu area lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥) — hearty pork rice soup, a local favorite (approx. ₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal BBQ dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Jongno — grill your own pork belly with banchan sides and soju (approx. ₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is a 5-minute walk from the boutique stay. Dress warmly — December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C typical). Consider renting a hanbok at the palace entrance for free admission and great photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Secret Garden tour is guided and limited in numbers; book in advance online (admission approx. ₩8,000). Stunning even in winter with snow-dusted pavilions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace next door (admission ₩1,000) and then stroll through the connected Jongmyo Shrine — the royal ancestral shrine, also a UNESCO site. The serene forested paths are peaceful in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions and the outdoor light installations. The surrounding Dongdaemun market area comes alive at night.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora or a local bakery in Insadong for a croissant and coffee (approx. ₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village nearby — a trendy alley with fusion Korean cafés; try a tteokbokki or bibimbap set lunch (approx. ₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest markets. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and eomuk (fish cake) from the street stalls (budget ₩10,000–15,000 for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Huwon Secret Garden tour online in advance at the official palace website. Gwangjang Market is a must for authentic street food culture — very popular with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park — take the subway to Gupabal Station (Line 3). Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail (moderate difficulty, approx. 3–4 hours round trip). Panoramic views of Seoul from the granite peaks are spectacular in clear winter weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Seochon Village (서촌) — the charming neighborhood west of Gyeongbokgung, full of indie cafés, art studios, and traditional alleyways. Visit Tong-Ui-Dong Bossam for a snack or explore the galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace at night if a special winter night opening is scheduled (check the palace website — occasional events in December). Otherwise, enjoy a relaxing evening in Seochon's café scene.

meals.breakfast: Early Korean convenience store breakfast or hotel — triangle kimbap and canned coffee for a quick pre-hike start (approx. ₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Pack a snack for the hike or eat at a mountain village restaurant near the trailhead — doenjang jjigae and rice (approx. ₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Seochon Village — try Jaha Son Mandu (자하손만두), a beloved dumpling restaurant known for handmade mandu (approx. ₩12,000–16,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking shoes and layer up for Bukhansan — trails can be icy in December. Crampons (아이젠) can be rented near the trailhead entrance for ₩3,000–5,000. Start the hike by 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hongdae (Hongik University area) — Seoul's youth culture and indie arts hub. Visit the street art walls, browse vinyl record shops, and explore the indie boutiques and character shops. Saturdays bring street performers and a lively market atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and then Yeonnam-dong — a trendy neighborhood with a linear park (Gyeongui Line Forest Park) lined with cafés and creative spaces. Perfect for a winter afternoon stroll and café hopping.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening — experience the nightlife district with live music venues, K-indie bands performing at small clubs, and neon-lit streets. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a Hongdae café — avocado toast or Korean egg sandwich with a specialty coffee (approx. ₩10,000–14,000)
meals.lunch: Hongdae street food: hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and odeng from pojangmacha (street stalls) (approx. ₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Gopchang (grilled intestines) or dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a mid-range Hongdae restaurant — a popular K-food experience (approx. ₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is about 30 minutes by subway from Gyeongbokgung (Line 3 to Line 2). Saturday is the best day to visit for the full street performance atmosphere. Norebang rooms cost approx. ₩15,000–25,000 per hour for a private room.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) — one of Korea's largest traditional markets open since 1414. Shop for Korean snacks, dried goods, clothing, and souvenirs. The market is especially vibrant on Sunday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Myeongdong — Seoul's famous shopping and beauty district. Browse K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), try street food along the main boulevard, and explore the department stores. Visit Myeongdong Cathedral, a beautiful Gothic landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Head to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) at dusk — take the cable car up for panoramic night views of the city. See the famous love lock fence and enjoy hot cocoa at the café with the glittering Seoul skyline below.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market breakfast — galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) and rice at a market restaurant, or hotteok from a street stall (approx. ₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — try Korean fried chicken skewers, egg bread (계란빵), and tornado potato (approx. ₩8,000–12,000 for a variety)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) — famous for their handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu, a Seoul institution (approx. ₩11,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car costs approx. ₩12,000 round trip. The tower observation deck is an additional ₩21,000. Arrive at dusk (around 5:30 PM in December) for the best transition from day to night views. Myeongdong is very crowded on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean art, history, and artifacts spanning 5,000 years. Free general admission. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Itaewon — Seoul's most international district. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (world-class contemporary and traditional Korean art, admission approx. ₩10,000) and browse the eclectic boutiques and antique shops on Antique Furniture Street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC) or Gyeongnidan-gil in Itaewon — trendy streets with international restaurants, craft beer bars, and a bohemian atmosphere. Great for an evening drink and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby Jongno café — Korean-style porridge (juk) at Bon Juk (본죽) for a warming winter breakfast (approx. ₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Museum café or nearby — bibimbap set at a restaurant near Yongsan (approx. ₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Gyeongnidan-gil restaurant — try a mid-range Korean-fusion spot or a traditional Korean restaurant. Hannam-dong area has excellent options (approx. ₩20,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is free and world-class — don't miss the Golden Crown of Silla and the Pensive Bodhisattva. Take subway Line 4 or Line 6 to reach Itaewon from the museum.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour south of Seoul by subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station, then bus). Walk the impressive fortress walls (total 5.7 km circuit), visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and enjoy the winter mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon — visit the Korean Folk Village nearby (Minsokchon) for traditional crafts, folk performances, and historical village life recreations. A great cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and relax in Insadong — browse the evening craft shops and enjoy a traditional tea ceremony experience at one of the tea houses.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near the hotel before departure — convenience store or local bakery (approx. ₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its large, meaty beef short ribs. Have lunch at a galbi restaurant near the fortress (approx. ₩20,000–25,000 per person, a worthwhile splurge)
meals.dinner: Insadong teahouse dinner — Sanchon (산촌) vegetarian temple food restaurant in Insadong, a unique cultural dining experience (approx. ₩25,000–30,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress admission is approx. ₩1,000. The Korean Folk Village admission is approx. ₩15,000. Check performance schedules in advance. The round trip to Suwon by subway costs approx. ₩5,000–7,000.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun History & Culture Park area and the nearby Heunginjimun Gate (East Gate) — one of Seoul's original city gates. Visit the DDP design museum exhibitions (admission varies by exhibit, approx. ₩5,000–10,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — an elevated highway converted into a beautiful urban stream promenade. Walk the 5.8 km path westward from Dongdaemun back toward Gwanghwamun, enjoying the winter light installations along the water.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve in Seoul — visit the festive Cheonggyecheon lantern displays and Gwanghwamun Square Christmas market. Seoul goes all out with holiday decorations. Enjoy mulled wine or hotteok at outdoor stalls.

meals.breakfast: Jongno-gu local breakfast — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a neighborhood restaurant (approx. ₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — try a quick dakgalbi or japchae at a local restaurant (approx. ₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area — enjoy dinner at Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae café area or a nearby Korean restaurant. Try haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake) and makgeolli (rice wine) — a classic Korean winter pairing (approx. ₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Cheonggyecheon Stream walk is flat and easy — about 1.5 hours at a leisurely pace. In December, the annual Lantern Festival lights may still be displayed along the stream. Dress warmly as the wind along the stream can be biting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, a 5-minute walk from the hotel. The temple is beautifully decorated with colorful lanterns in winter. Attend a morning bell ceremony if available. Then visit the nearby Unhyeongung Palace (free admission).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Korean traditional craft scene at the Bukchon area — visit the Gahoe Museum (traditional folk art) and browse the hanok galleries. Try a traditional craft workshop: hanji (Korean paper) making or celadon pottery painting (approx. ₩20,000–30,000 for workshops).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — Myeongdong Cathedral holds a beautiful midnight mass (free, all welcome). Before the service, enjoy the festive Myeongdong Christmas market atmosphere, carol singers, and spectacular building light displays. A magical Seoul experience.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve brunch — visit a nice café in Seochon or Bukchon for a festive spread (approx. ₩15,000–20,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Insadong — tteok (rice cake) desserts and traditional snacks from the market stalls (approx. ₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Festive Christmas Eve dinner at a mid-range Korean restaurant — try a special set menu. Jungsik Diner or a quality Korean BBQ restaurant in Jongno (approx. ₩30,000–40,000 per person for a Christmas splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is widely celebrated in Seoul — the city is beautifully decorated. Myeongdong Cathedral's Christmas Eve mass is a popular and moving experience. Book dinner reservations in advance as Christmas Eve is very busy in Seoul restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) — a scenic island about 1.5 hours from Seoul, famous for its beautiful tree-lined paths and K-drama filming locations (Winter Sonata). Take the ITX train from Cheongnyangni Station to Gapyeong, then a ferry to the island (total approx. ₩25,000–30,000 round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Nami Island — walk the iconic metasequoia and birch tree lanes (stunning in winter with frost or snow), visit the art installations, and enjoy the peaceful island atmosphere. Combine with a visit to Petite France or the Garden of Morning Calm nearby if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and enjoy a quiet Christmas evening in the Insadong or Seochon area — warm up with a hot drink at a cozy café and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go — convenience store breakfast before the train (approx. ₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Nami Island restaurants — the island has several dining options including Korean BBQ and set meals (approx. ₩15,000–20,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner back in Seoul — try a traditional Korean jeongsik (set course meal) at a restaurant in Jongno-gu (approx. ₩25,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island admission (including ferry) is approx. ₩16,000. Christmas Day is a public holiday in Korea — most attractions remain open but book train tickets in advance. The island is magical in winter, especially if there's snow.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gangnam district — take the subway to Apgujeong or Sinsa Station. Explore Garosu-gil (가로수길), a tree-lined boulevard with high-end boutiques, concept stores, and the best street café culture in Seoul. Browse K-fashion and beauty flagship stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. See the famous COEX Library (a stunning public library-bookstore hybrid, free entry) and explore the aquarium (approx. ₩29,000) or the SM Town COEX Artium for K-pop merchandise and exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Banpo Bridge area at sunset — watch the famous Moonlight Rainbow Fountain show (check seasonal schedule; may not operate in deep winter). Walk along the Hangang River waterfront. Return to Gangnam for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Trendy Garosu-gil café brunch — eggs benedict or açaí bowl at a stylish café (approx. ₩15,000–18,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court — excellent variety of Korean food options at reasonable prices (approx. ₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam-gu dinner — try Jungsik (중식) or a quality Korean BBQ restaurant in the Apgujeong area; galbi (beef short ribs) for a final big-night meal (approx. ₩25,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The COEX Starfield Library is free and absolutely stunning — a must-visit even for non-readers. Gangnam is about 40 minutes by subway from Gyeongbokgung (Line 3 to Line 2). Saturday in Garosu-gil is very lively with weekend shoppers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning stroll around Gyeongbokgung neighborhood — visit the nearby Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds one last time for a farewell view. Stop at a local café for a final Korean breakfast. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at Insadong or the hotel area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head to Incheon Airport — take the AREX Express Train from Seoul Station (recommended: depart by 2:00–3:00 PM for an evening flight, adjust based on actual flight time). Use duty-free shopping at the airport for final Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, incredible food, and Seoul's unique blend of ancient tradition and ultra-modern energy.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — go back to Tosokchon for one last bowl of samgyetang, or try a traditional Korean set meal (백반, baekban) at a neighborhood restaurant (approx. ₩10,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Airport lunch at Incheon — the airport has excellent Korean food options including proper restaurant-quality bibimbap and doenjang jjigae (approx. ₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Incheon Airport check-in, immigration, and security. The AREX Express from Seoul Station takes 43 minutes. Consider using the City Airport Terminal in Jongno (AREX City Check-in) to check luggage in advance and clear immigration before heading to the airport — saves significant time.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from ICN to boutique hotel in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu (approx. 60–70 min by premium chauffeur service).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to boutique stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely evening stroll through the UNESCO-listed Bukchon Hanok Village, just minutes from the hotel — winding alleys of traditional Korean hanok houses offer a stunning first impression of Seoul's heritage. Browse nearby Insadong's artisan galleries and traditional craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Jungsik (2 Michelin stars, Gangnam) or opt for closer fine dining at Balwoo Gongyang, a celebrated temple food restaurant near Gyeongbokgung — a serene and deeply Korean first-night experience.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: N/A (still in transit)
meals.dinner: Balwoo Gongyang — upscale Korean Buddhist temple cuisine with seasonal vegetarian tasting menu; reservations essential

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance with a premium chauffeur service such as KKday VIP Transfer or hotel concierge. Dress warmly — December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C). Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Gyeongbokgung Palace opening ceremony (Changing of the Royal Guard at 10:00 & 14:00). Explore the grand palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon throne hall, Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea adjacent to Gyeongbokgung for exquisite Joseon Dynasty artifacts. Then head to Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence opened to the public — for a guided premium tour of its gardens and historic halls.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the beautifully illuminated Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade. Dinner in the upscale Gwanghwamun or Samcheong-dong neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or nearby Café Bora (famous for purple latte and Korean pastries) in Bukchon
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — iconic ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, beloved for centuries
meals.dinner: Mingles (1 Michelin star, Gangnam) or Dooreyoo — modern Korean cuisine with exceptional seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is walkable from the hotel. Wear layered clothing for outdoor palace exploration. Consider renting a hanbok (traditional dress) at the palace entrance for complimentary admission and stunning photos.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Changdeokgung Palace and its legendary Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The garden is especially atmospheric in winter with frost-dusted pavilions and frozen ponds. Book a premium private guide for exclusive storytelling of the Joseon court.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Changgyeonggung Palace and the adjacent Jongmyo Shrine — the oldest royal Confucian shrine in the world, serene and profoundly moving. Walk through the pine-lined paths in meditative quiet.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for a curated K-culture experience: visit Ssamziegil courtyard complex for contemporary Korean art and design. Dinner at a traditional Korean fine dining establishment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café de Paris near Anguk Station — French-Korean fusion bakery beloved by locals
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market (10 min away) — premium street food experience: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare) served at the best stalls
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan — one of Seoul's oldest and most prestigious Korean restaurants serving royal court cuisine (hansik) in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are timed and ticketed — book in advance. Jongmyo Shrine is only open to independent visitors on weekdays; weekends require joining a guided tour group. Dress in warm layers.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersive K-culture morning: private Hanbok styling session at a premium hanbok atelier in Bukchon (e.g., Hanboknam or Leesle), followed by a traditional Korean tea ceremony at a historic hanok teahouse such as Cha Masineun Ttul in Insadong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (20 min by taxi) — one of Asia's largest museums housing 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric to Joseon eras. Explore at a leisurely, unhurried pace.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) at dusk for panoramic city views. Take the private cable car up, then enjoy cocktails at the N Grill revolving restaurant atop the tower.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast (juk — rice porridge) at Bonjuk near Insadong, or in-hotel
meals.lunch: Museum restaurant or nearby Itaewon fine dining — Vatos Urban Tacos for a fun Korean-Mexican fusion, or La Yeon (The Shilla Hotel, 3 Michelin stars) for the ultimate Korean fine dining lunch
meals.dinner: N Grill at Namsan Tower — revolving panoramic restaurant with Korean-Western fusion; reserve a window table for city views

day_by_day.notes: La Yeon requires advance reservations weeks ahead. The Namsan cable car can be crowded on Friday evenings — consider arriving before 17:30 for sunset views. Namsan is accessible by taxi from Insadong in 15 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) with a premium private guided tour — one of the most compelling geopolitical experiences in the world. Visit the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station. Book through a reputable operator like Koridoor or USO.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul by mid-afternoon. Rest or explore the upscale boutiques and galleries of Samcheong-dong neighborhood — a charming mix of contemporary art galleries, independent design stores, and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the trendy Seochon Village (just west of Gyeongbokgung) — an area favored by Seoul's creative class with intimate restaurants and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before 07:30 departure for DMZ
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box provided by tour operator, or lunch at Dorasan Station area
meals.dinner: Dooreyoo or Evett (Seochon) — intimate modern Korean tasting menu in a beautifully restored hanok setting

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours require passport. Book at least 2 weeks in advance as JSA access requires US military approval. Tours typically depart by 08:00 and return by 15:00–16:00. Dress in warm, conservative clothing (no camouflage patterns allowed at JSA).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Namdaemun Market (Korea's largest traditional market) for a vibrant Sunday morning immersion — browse ginseng, dried seafood, street food, and traditional goods. Then visit nearby Deoksugung Palace with its Western-style stone hall and changing of the guard ceremony (10:30 & 14:30).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Deoksugung Stonewall Walkway — a romantically tree-lined path. Head to the Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) adjacent to the palace for contemporary Korean and international art exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the sophisticated Cheongdam-dong and Apgujeong district in Gangnam — Seoul's most luxurious shopping enclave. Browse flagship stores of Korean luxury brands like MCM, Gentle Monster, and Ader Error.

meals.breakfast: Street breakfast at Namdaemun Market — hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and fish cake skewers
meals.lunch: Mingles (Gangnam, 1 Michelin star) — modern Korean cuisine blending traditional hansik with global techniques; exceptional wine pairing available
meals.dinner: Dosa (Apgujeong) or Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — Korea's pinnacle of fine dining; multi-course royal court cuisine in an exquisite setting

day_by_day.notes: Gaon requires reservations 1–2 months in advance and is widely considered the best Korean fine dining experience in the country. Dress code is smart elegant. Namdaemun Market is liveliest in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-pop and Hallyu culture deep-dive: Visit SM Town COEX Artium in Gangnam — an immersive K-pop entertainment complex with exhibitions, hologram theaters, and exclusive merchandise. Then explore the SMTOWN Museum and attend a hologram concert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit COEX Mall and the iconic COEX Library (Starfield Library) — one of Seoul's most photographed spaces with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves. Explore the K-wave exhibition at the nearby Korea Tourism Organization's Hallyu Experience Center.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live K-pop performance or music show recording (apply for audience tickets in advance through Naver or Melon). Alternatively, experience a Nanta performance — Korea's award-winning non-verbal percussion show — at the Nanta Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or trendy Gangnam café — % Arabica or Fritz Coffee Company for specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Bongeunsa Temple food café near COEX for a mindful break, or upscale Korean BBQ at Maple Tree House (Itaewon) — premium wagyu and Korean beef cuts
meals.dinner: Jungsik (2 Michelin stars, Gangnam) — Korean-inspired contemporary tasting menu; one of Seoul's most celebrated restaurants

day_by_day.notes: K-pop show recordings are free but require advance online applications (often 1–2 weeks prior). Check Mnet, KBS, or SBS websites. COEX is accessible from Gangnam Station. Evening Nanta show tickets should be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 45 minutes from Seoul by KTX or private car. Walk the 5.7km fortress walls with stunning winter views, visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and explore the traditional Suwon folk village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul and explore the vibrant Hongdae neighborhood — Seoul's creative and youth culture hub. Visit independent art galleries, street murals, vinyl record shops, and the Trick Eye Museum for immersive art experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hongdae's legendary nightlife: rooftop bars, live indie music venues, and the famous busking performances near Hongdae Park.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (grilled short ribs) at Yeonpo Galbi in Suwon — Suwon is nationally famous for its galbi; a must-eat experience
meals.dinner: Hongdae neighborhood dinner at Palsaik Samgyeopsal — 8-flavored pork belly BBQ in a lively, authentic setting; or upscale option at Kum San (Mapo-gu)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is best reached by private car or KTX (Suwon Station then taxi). The fortress wall walk takes 2–3 hours. Wear very warm footwear — fortress paths can be icy in December. Hongdae busking performances are typically from 18:00–22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a master chef specializing in royal Korean cuisine (hansik) — learn to prepare kimchi, japchae, galbi, and traditional banchan (side dishes). Several premium culinary schools near Insadong and Anguk offer bespoke experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kimchi Museum (Pulmuone Kimchi Museum) or the National Intangible Heritage Center for a deeper dive into Korea's living cultural traditions — UNESCO-recognized intangible heritage including music, dance, and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performing arts show: Jeongdong Theater near Deoksugung Palace offers nightly performances of traditional music (gugak), dance, and mask drama (talchum) in a beautiful heritage theater.

meals.breakfast: Korean-style hotel breakfast or Gyeongbokgung area café
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your morning cooking class
meals.dinner: Jirisan (Insadong) or Sanchon — celebrated restaurant serving traditional mountain monk cuisine in a hanok setting with live traditional music performances during dinner

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one week in advance — recommended providers include O'ngo Food Communications or Korean Food Foundation premium experiences. Jeongdong Theater performances run nightly (except Mondays); book tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lotte World Tower and Sky31 observation deck in Jamsil — one of the world's tallest buildings with breathtaking views of Seoul. Visit the Lotte World Museum of Art for world-class exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Olympic Park (Songpa-gu) — beautifully decorated for Christmas and winter. Visit the SOMA Museum of Art within the park and enjoy the peaceful lakeside atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special experience: Seoul is festively decorated in December. Enjoy the Cheonggyecheon Stream Christmas light festival, then a spectacular Christmas Eve dinner at one of Seoul's top fine dining venues.

meals.breakfast: Lotte Hotel buffet breakfast or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Bongpiyang (Songpa-gu) — premium Korean BBQ near Olympic Park using premium Hanwoo beef (Korea's finest wagyu-equivalent)
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve tasting menu at La Yeon (The Shilla Hotel, 3 Michelin stars) or Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul (Lotte Hotel) — French haute cuisine by legendary chef Pierre Gagnaire

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is extremely festive — Myeongdong and Cheonggyecheon are beautifully illuminated. Book Christmas Eve dinner reservations at least 3–4 weeks in advance as Seoul's top restaurants fill up quickly. Consider a festive cocktail at the rooftop bar of The Shilla or Park Hyatt Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning: visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in Jongno-gu, just minutes from the hotel. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and offers a tranquil contrast to the festive city. Attend a morning prayer ceremony if desired.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Hannam-dong neighborhood — Seoul's most cosmopolitan district with luxury boutiques, contemporary art galleries (Pace Gallery Seoul, Kukje Gallery), and beautiful cafés. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art for world-class Korean and international art.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day sunset at Bukhansan National Park viewpoint (accessible by taxi — Bukhansanseong area) for panoramic winter views over Seoul. Then a celebratory Christmas dinner.

meals.breakfast: Festive hotel Christmas breakfast
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong café dining — Café Onion Hannam (beautifully designed café in a converted warehouse) for brunch plates and artisan coffee
meals.dinner: Ryunique (Gangnam) — avant-garde Korean fine dining with theatrical presentation; or Evett for a more intimate, seasonal Christmas tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Leeum Museum requires advance ticket booking. Bukhansan viewpoint is best at 16:00–17:00 for winter sunset views. Most venues operate on Christmas Day in Seoul — it is celebrated but not a major public holiday in the Western sense.

day_by_day.morning: Premium spa and wellness morning: indulge in a traditional Korean jjimjilbang experience at Dragon Hill Spa (Yongsan) — a luxury 24-hour Korean bathhouse with multiple themed sauna rooms, hot spring baths, and relaxation lounges. Or opt for a premium spa treatment at The Shilla Hotel spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final shopping and souvenir experience: visit Gwangjang Market for premium Korean traditional goods (hanji paper, silk, antiques), then explore Insadong's finest art galleries and ceramics shops. Visit Kyobo Bookstore in Gwanghwamun for beautiful Korean stationery and cultural books.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Seoul's most iconic fine dining experience — a final celebration of Korean culinary excellence.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take time to savor the final mornings
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market premium lunch: fresh raw beef (yukhoe), bindaetteok, and silken tofu stew — an authentic Seoul market feast
meals.dinner: Gaon (3 Michelin stars) or La Yeon (3 Michelin stars) — the ultimate farewell dinner celebrating Korean royal court cuisine with impeccable service and full tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours; weekends can be busy — arrive by 10:00. Book farewell dinner reservations well in advance. Consider purchasing premium Korean gifts: red ginseng products (Korea Ginseng Corp), premium dried seaweed sets, traditional celadon ceramics, and artisan soju.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul: wake early for a last peaceful walk through Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds at dawn — the palace is magical in the early winter morning light with minimal crowds. Stop at a neighborhood café for a final Korean coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from hotel. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport (allow 90 minutes for comfortable arrival). Enjoy the world-class Incheon Airport duty-free shopping — one of the best airport retail experiences in the world (Korean cosmetics, fashion, electronics, and gourmet food).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast: haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty beef bone broth soup) at a local neighborhood restaurant near the hotel — a beloved Korean morning tradition
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport premium dining — Korean BBQ or bibimbap at one of the excellent airport restaurants in Terminal 1 or 2
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Check out by hotel's designated time (typically 11:00–12:00). Incheon Airport is consistently rated the world's best airport — arrive at least 3 hours before international departure. Korean duty-free is exceptional — purchase Korean skincare (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo), premium teas, and gourmet snacks as final gifts. Ensure all receipts are ready for VAT refund at the airport.
